svg.title: How go-wal works
svg.desc: Concurrent appends go through a single writer that assigns LSNs, fsyncs once per batch and writes CRC32C-framed records into size-rolled segment files. A follower tails committed records and Truncate deletes old segments.
svg.text: go-wal · how an append becomes durable

g.text: 1 · Concurrent Append() calls are queued for one writer goroutine
2 · The writer batches them and assigns monotonic, gapless LSNs
3 · Each batch is written, fsync'd once (group commit), then acked
4 · The follower was blocked at the tail. It wakes and reads 9–11
5 · LSN 12 fills the segment, so the log rolls to a new file
6 · Appends continue in the new active segment, with no LSN gap
7 · Truncate(9) deletes the whole closed segments below LSN 9

svg.text: segment header: Magic · Version · Flags · BaseLSN · CreatedAt · CRC
On Open, recovery truncates a torn tail, resumes at LastLSN+1.
